VibePascal v58 -- arm-linux CROSS compiler -- runs on x86_64-linux, emits 32-bit arm-linux
Source commit: dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a
Parent release for THIS target: v54 (b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e)
Built: 2026-09-11 on x86_64-linux, from a CLEAN compiler/arm unit tree, driven by
       the v58 native ppcx64 (md5 8c8179b2f0a452cebec0131aa301b076), -dFPC_ARMHF
Binary: bin/ppcrossarm  md5 5e3d9ba2d978db06b31a1a15c37244d9
                        sha256 5d819aa301ecd888015b7804e75fb6cdb73f2c2464fe2537e180aa5757ce03f4
                        5342672 bytes, ELF 64-bit x86-64, statically linked, stripped

ABI: ARMHF (ARM EABI5, HARD float / VFP) -- the ABI of 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS and
of Debian/Ubuntu armhf.  It is NOT compatible with an armel (soft-float) system.
The tree's own default is armel (compiler/fpcdefs.inc:249), so this build passes
-dFPC_ARMHF explicitly; unchanged from the v54 cross compiler it replaces.

THIS TARGET WAS FOUR RELEASES BEHIND.  x86_64 shipped v55, v56, v57 and v58 while
this cross compiler stayed on v54, so it collects everything in between:

  v55 (4d10b26fe7)  a missing -FU/-FE output directory is CREATED instead of
                    complained about.
  v56 (f06e46d8eb)  an inferred inline var initialised from a real constant is a
                    Double, whatever the constant's value happens to be.
  v57 (c31227c8ca)  a half-written .ppu is an ERROR, not an infinite 99%-CPU spin
                    with no message.
  v58 (dedf242c69)  a .ppu SHORTER than the length its own header declares is
                    rejected instead of silently accepted.

Nothing in the RTL, the packages or the PPU format changed across v54..v58, so an
existing arm-linux unit set stays valid and does not need rebuilding.

VERIFIED ON THESE EXACT BYTES
-----------------------------
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh ppcrossarm arm-linux, against the real
    54211-byte packages/aspell/units/arm-linux/aspelldyn.ppu:
        11/25 offsets clean, 14 problem(s), exit 1   on the v54 binary this replaces
        25/25 offsets clean,  0 problem(s), exit 0   on this one
    Of the 14: 9 truncations HUNG and had to be killed at 30s, and 5 were
    ACCEPTED with rc=0 -- a corrupt unit taken as valid, silently.
    The pre-fix binary is the one that actually shipped as v54, preserved and
    re-run this cycle -- not a reconstruction.
  * EXECUTION, not inspection: this compiler built tests/test/tinlinevarnativeint1.pp
    -Munleashed into an ELF 32-bit ARM EABI5 hard-float binary which RAN under
    qemu-arm-static and reported checks=45 fails=0 NativeInt=4, VERDICT:PASS.

BUILD PROVENANCE, because a cross build can lie about being one
---------------------------------------------------------------
An incremental build of this target against the Sep-10 unit tree did not merely
reuse stale units -- it CRASHED the driver compiler with an access violation
while compiling pp.pas.  Wiping compiler/arm/{bin,units} and rebuilding from
scratch fixed it with no source change.  241 units were recompiled for this
binary; if you are reproducing it, check that count rather than the timestamps.

NOT PROVEN HERE: qemu-user is an emulator.  It runs the real shipped bytes and
real ARM encodings, so codegen and RTL defects do surface, but it is not a
Raspberry Pi.  Nobody has run this compiler's output on physical ARM silicon.
